name: RD-107 / RD-108
tagline: Sputnik's engine — still flying humans 65 years later
description: The RD-107 and RD-108 are the engines of the R-7, the world's first intercontinental ballistic missile, which Sergei Korolev's team repurposed as a launch vehicle. The RD-107 powers the R-7's four strap-on boosters; the RD-108 drives the sustainer core. Both run a gas-generator cycle on LOX and kerosene, and both first flew on 21 August 1957 — months before Sputnik. Upgraded as the RD-107A and RD-108A, they continue to power Soyuz rockets carrying crews to the International Space Station, making them the longest-operating human-rated propulsion system in history.
best_known_for: The R-7 engines — still flying humans on Soyuz after 65+ years
